author: Dhruv
before: The dhruv branch had no report builder. Auth guard, dropdown and customer DTO matched the earlier dhruv state.
after: The merge brings in dev's report builder (fields, query, saved templates), a customReports table with a ReportType enum, a WEEK_OFF attendance value, auth guard message constants and comments, and a hardcoded Report Builder module in the designation modules dropdown.
effects: New /reports/builder endpoints read loan overview data
New customReports table needs a schema push
getModules in the dropdown service changed what menu-rights screens receive
Attendance status enum gains WEEK_OFF

findings.title: Report data endpoints had no page right or branch scope
findings.problem: At the merge, every /reports/builder route used only AuthGuard. Any logged-in employee could POST /query for loan data of all branches and products, and read other employees' saved reports.
findings.impact: Cross-branch loan data exposure to any employee.
findings.fix: Add RequirePageRight and scope runs by the employee's access configuration.
findings.resolvedNote: Marked resolved manually

findings.title: Hardcoded fake Report Builder module pushed into designation modules
findings.problem: getModules appended a module with a made-up id to every designation's module list. getMenuRights and the menu-rights screens use this list, so a module that is not in the database appeared there.
findings.impact: Menu-rights screens show a phantom module that cannot be saved against; ids not in master_menu_modules.
findings.fix: Remove the hardcoded module and seed the real one in the database.
findings.resolvedNote: getModules now returns only database modules (dropdown.service.ts:541-543).

findings.title: Column names built with sql.raw string concatenation, and IsIn with raw values
findings.problem: Selected columns were turned into SQL with sql.raw of a template string, and the DTO validated keys with IsIn(REPORT_COLUMN_KEYS). Both break CLAUDE.md rules, and the raw string depended on a registry staying trusted.
findings.impact: Injection risk if the registry ever takes outside input; rule violation.
findings.fix: Use sql.identifier and enum or id-based validation.
findings.resolvedNote: report-builder.query.ts:23-24 uses sql.identifier and fields come from the database by id.

findings.title: Noisy or misspelled comments added against the comment rule
findings.problem: The merge adds comments such as a question about returning early, 'prioritize wich every found first' and a question about a table in accounts.ts. They explain no business or technical reason, and CLAUDE.md says to remove noisy comments.
findings.impact: Noise and typos in guard and schema code; no runtime effect.
findings.fix: Remove them or turn them into issues.
findings.evidence:
//is it good to just return ?
//prioritize wich every found first

findings.title: Aggregation row always returns 0
findings.problem: buildAggregationRow returns { name, value: 0 } for every aggregated column without querying anything. This was added after the merge (cd07ebd1) and is in the current code.
findings.impact: A report with a SUM or COUNT column shows a total of 0 next to rows with real values.
findings.fix: Compute the aggregation in SQL, or omit the row until it is implemented.

findings.title: Physical table and column names typed inside raw SQL
findings.problem: Filters use sql with typed names such as the lao loanDate, branchId and la loanCloseDate columns. CLAUDE.md says to interpolate Drizzle column objects instead of typing names.
findings.impact: A column rename in the view or table breaks the report at runtime, not at compile time.
findings.fix: Reference loanApplicationOverviewView and loanApplicationsTable columns through Drizzle aliases.

author: Dhruv
before: The consumer UCRF report wrote one short TUDF record per loan with simple segment tags, a single phone and ID list, and no old account, income, email or secondary address data. With closed cases included it reported open loans together with loans closed in the chosen window.
after: The TUDF builder emits segment-length tags (PN03, ID03, PT03, EC03, PA03, TL04), up to five name fields, several phones, emails, a secondary address, old account number, interest rate and income fields, and the grid shows old account and NREGA/CKYC data. With closed cases included the filter returns open loans plus loans closed between the closed-from date and the reporting date.
effects: UCRF consumer TUDF file content and field order for every reported loan
UCRF consumer grid and Excel export columns (old account number column key renamed)
Loan selection for the UCRF report when includeClosedCases is true
NREGA and CKYC document lookups that depend on two new master document IDs
generate-ucrf-report requests that set includeClosedCases without closedFromDate now fail with 400

findings.title: Including closed cases drops every open loan
findings.problem: buildLoanPortfolioFilter builds openLoanFilters, returns them only when includeClosedCases is false, and otherwise returns and(...closedLoanFilters). The previous or(open, closed) is gone, so with includeClosedCases=true the open filters are built and thrown away.
findings.impact: A report generated with 'include closed cases' contains only closed loans. The live portfolio is missing from the file submitted to the bureau, and the grid shows the wrong set.
findings.fix: Return or(and(...openLoanFilters), and(...closedLoanFilters)) when includeClosedCases is true, and import or again.
findings.resolvedNote: Marked resolved manually

findings.title: Loans closed after the reporting date are reported as closed
findings.problem: The closed filter no longer has lte(loanCloseDate, reportingDate). It only requires loanCloseDate >= closedFromDate, so a loan closed after the reporting date matches.
findings.impact: For a back-dated reporting date, such a loan is written with a closed status code and a Date Closed later than the reporting date, although it was still open on that date.
findings.fix: Keep lte(loanApplicationsTable.loanCloseDate, reportingDateSql) in the closed filter next to the gte on closedFromDate.
findings.resolvedNote: ucrf-report.service.ts:1361-1364 bounds loanCloseDate below the day after the reporting date.

findings.title: NREGA id gets the string 'null' when last name is empty
findings.problem: row.lastName is typed string | null and is concatenated onto the NREGA number with +. A null last name produces '<card>null'.
findings.impact: The identifier written to the bureau file is corrupted for any customer with an NREGA card and no last name, and a long card number can be cut by the 30 character limit.
findings.fix: Append the last name only when it is present, for example number: row.nregaCard + (row.lastName ?? ''), or confirm with the spec that the name must be appended at all.
findings.evidence: ids.push({ type: TUDF_ID_TYPE.NREGA, number: row.nregaCard + row.lastName })
findings.resolvedNote: lib/consumer/tudf-file.builder.ts:141 uses (row.lastName ?? '') instead of concatenating null.

findings.title: Field 38 written empty when interest rate is null
findings.problem: formatInterestRate returns '' for a null rate and buildVarField turns that into the zero-length field '3800'. The field is also gated on noOfInstallments instead of on the rate.
findings.impact: Loans with installments but no IRR get an empty field 38 that the bureau can reject, and loans with a rate but no installment count never report it.
findings.fix: Gate the field on row.interestRate being present and non-null, not on noOfInstallments.
findings.resolvedNote: lib/consumer/tudf-file.builder.ts:376-379 writes field 38 only when formatInterestRate returns a value.

findings.title: New NREGA and CKYC master document ids look like placeholders
findings.problem: The two ids follow a sequential pattern unlike the neighbouring generated ids, and nothing else in the repo references them. If no master document row exists with these ids, the lookups always return null.
findings.impact: NREGA and CKYC numbers are silently never reported, which looks the same as customers having no such document.
findings.fix: Confirm both ids exist in the master documents table (or add the seed) and replace them with the real ids.
findings.resolvedNote: Marked resolved manually
findings.confirmedNote: Confirmed manually: NREGA and CKYC ids exist in the documents table (checked against the project database).

findings.title: Grid row DTO not updated for the renamed old account column
findings.problem: TUcrfConsumerGridRow and UCRF_CONSUMER_GRID_COLUMNS now use oldAccountNumber, but UcrfConsumerGridRowDto still declares only oldAccountNo, so the Swagger schema has no oldAccountNumber field.
findings.impact: Clients generated from the API schema do not see the new Old Acc No column key, and oldAccountNo is still sent as a duplicate.
findings.fix: Add oldAccountNumber to the DTO and drop the unused oldAccountNo, or keep the old key in the column list.
findings.resolvedNote: dto/ucrf-consumer-grid-row.dto.ts:85 declares oldAccountNumber, and oldAccountNo is gone from the types and mapper.

findings.title: Grid account type lost its default while the file keeps it
findings.problem: The grid now shows row.cibilAccountTypeCode as is, but the TUDF builder still writes (row.cibilAccountTypeCode ?? '05').padStart(2, '0') at tudf-file.builder.ts:346.
findings.impact: For a product with no CIBIL type the grid shows a blank account type while the submitted file says 05, so what the user reviews differs from what is sent.
findings.fix: Use the same default and padding in the grid, or remove the default from the file builder.
findings.resolvedNote: lib/consumer/ucrf-consumer-grid.mapper.ts:90 applies the same 05 default and 2-digit padding as the file builder.

author: Dhruv
before: The consumer UCRF report wrote one short TUDF record per loan with simple segment tags, a single phone and ID list, and no old account, income, email or secondary address data. With closed cases included it reported open loans together with loans closed in the chosen window.
after: The TUDF builder emits segment-length tags (PN03, ID03, PT03, EC03, PA03, TL04), up to five name fields, several phones, emails, a secondary address, old account number, interest rate and income fields, and the grid shows Account Name-less old account and NREGA/CKYC data. With closed cases included the portfolio filter now returns only closed loans.
effects: UCRF consumer TUDF file content and field order for every reported loan
UCRF consumer grid and Excel export columns (old account number column key renamed)
Loan selection for the UCRF report when includeClosedCases is true
NREGA and CKYC document lookups that depend on two new master document IDs
generate-ucrf-report requests that set includeClosedCases without closedFromDate now fail with 400

findings.title: Including closed cases drops every open loan
findings.problem: buildLoanPortfolioFilter builds openLoanFilters, returns them only when includeClosedCases is false, and otherwise returns and(...closedLoanFilters). The previous or(open, closed) is gone, so with includeClosedCases=true the open filters are built and thrown away.
findings.impact: A report generated with 'include closed cases' contains only closed loans. The live portfolio is missing from the file submitted to the bureau, and the grid shows the wrong set.
findings.fix: Return or(and(...openLoanFilters), and(...closedLoanFilters)) when includeClosedCases is true, and import or again.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: the filter returns or(open, closed) when closed cases are included at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/ucrf-report.service.ts:1372.

findings.title: Loans closed after the reporting date are reported as closed
findings.problem: The closed filter no longer has lte(loanCloseDate, reportingDate). It only requires loanCloseDate >= closedFromDate, so a loan closed after the reporting date matches.
findings.impact: For a back-dated reporting date, such a loan is written with a closed status code and a Date Closed later than the reporting date, although it was still open on that date.
findings.fix: Keep lte(loanApplicationsTable.loanCloseDate, reportingDateSql) in the closed filter next to the gte on closedFromDate.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: closed loans are bounded to closedFromDate through the reporting date, inclusive, at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/ucrf-report.service.ts:1363.

findings.title: NREGA id gets the string 'null' when last name is empty
findings.problem: row.lastName is typed string | null and is concatenated onto the NREGA number with +. A null last name produces '<card>null'.
findings.impact: The identifier written to the bureau file is corrupted for any customer with an NREGA card and no last name, and a long card number can be cut by the 30 character limit.
findings.fix: Append the last name only when it is present, for example number: row.nregaCard + (row.lastName ?? ''), or confirm with the spec that the name must be appended at all.
findings.evidence: ids.push({ type: TUDF_ID_TYPE.NREGA, number: row.nregaCard + row.lastName })
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: the last name is appended only when present at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/lib/consumer/tudf-file.builder.ts:141.

findings.title: Field 38 written empty when interest rate is null
findings.problem: formatInterestRate returns '' for a null rate and buildVarField turns that into the zero-length field '3800'. The field is also gated on noOfInstallments instead of on the rate.
findings.impact: Loans with installments but no IRR get an empty field 38 that the bureau can reject, and loans with a rate but no installment count never report it.
findings.fix: Gate the field on row.interestRate being present and non-null, not on noOfInstallments.
findings.resolvedNote: Fixed: field 38 is written whenever a rate exists, not only with installments, at apps/finnaux-api/src/reports/ucrf-report/lib/consumer/tudf-file.builder.ts:378.

findings.title: New NREGA and CKYC master document ids look like placeholders
findings.problem: The two ids follow a sequential pattern unlike the neighbouring generated ids, and nothing else in the repo references them. If no master document row exists with these ids, the lookups always return null.
findings.impact: NREGA and CKYC numbers are silently never reported, which looks the same as customers having no such document.
findings.fix: Confirm both ids exist in the master documents table (or add the seed) and replace them with the real ids.
findings.resolvedNote: Marked resolved manually
findings.confirmedNote: Confirmed manually: NREGA and CKYC ids exist in the documents table (checked against the project database).
